violation_type.title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio (26 TAC §744.1601)
violation_type.typical_finding: The operation exceeded the maximum group size for two or more caregivers.

finding_variants.text: The operation exceeded the maximum group size for two or more caregivers.
Inspector observed one staff with 46 children on two different occasions during the inspection.     Inspector also observed another staff with over 35 children during the inspection.

At time of inspection sole caregiver in the cafeteria was observed with 30 children with a specified age group of 6 years old. Caregiver was over ratio by 4 children.     This was corrected at inspection when a second caregiver was added.

Upon arrival, two caregivers were observed with a total of 42 children, 5-9 years of age. The children were observed in an open gym area, and outdoor area.  At 4:13PM, a total of 33 children were observed in care with two staff.  At 4:18PM, a total of 29 children, 5-9 years of age were observed with Staff B.

There were 39 children supervised by two caregivers. The caregivers could not step out to release children to parents or supervise children in the restroom without exceeding the maximum ratio of 26 children to one caregiver.
A caregiver was over ratio by 3 children.This was corrected when another caregiver took 2 children from this group and 1 child when home.

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio: The deficiency is related to a DFPS Abuse/Neglect investigation.
Child/ Caregiver Ratio: The amount of children one caregiver is allowed to supervise at one time exceed the childcare ratio of 26. There were 28 children in the room.
Child/ Caregiver Ratio: The operations has two caregivers present with a total of 44 children.
Child/ Caregiver Ratio: This standard was evaluated in regard to an investigation and a violation was found. A caregiver was left by themselves with 30 children.

Child/ Caregiver Ratio: There were 2 groups of 50 children in care this afternoon.    The program was out of ratio from 3:25 PM to 3:45 PM, one caregiver was taking care of 28 children in one group:    2 children : 3  y/o.  2 children : 4  y/o.  12 children : 5 y/o.  9 children : 6 y/o.  3 children : 7 y/o.    At 3:45 PM the site director moved three 7 y/o children and one 6 y/o child to the other group of 22 children from 9 y/o to 12 y/o. Two 3 y/o children left at 3:40 PM.    At 3:45 PM there were 2 groups of children in care:    One group of 26 children from 6-12 yo with one caregiver, and 1 group of 22 children from 4-6 y/o (12 children of 5 y/o).
Child/ Caregiver Ratio: I observed one caregiver supervising a group of 56 children in the cafeteria.

Child/ Caregiver Ratio: One caregiver was left with 27 children during the inspection. The caregiver was over in ratios by 1 child an additional caregiver was needed.     Note: A caregiver was added to the group during the inspection.
Child/ Caregiver Ratio: Based on information gathered during the investigation, it was determined that the operation is not adhering to the required child-to-caregiver ratio.

Child/ Caregiver Ratio: One caregiver was in charge of 50 children for the first hour of operation. The maximum capacity for a group with a specified age group of 6-8yo for one caregiver is 26. This group is over by 24 children. Note: this was corrected at inspection when the second caregiver arrived, divided the large group and both groups operated in ratio.

Child/ Caregiver Ratio: When I first got here, there was only one caregiver with 27 students ages 4-11 years old.  There was one caregiver in the restroom with 3 children. Also, one caregiver had to continue to leave the room, go down the hall, out the door, and about 30 feet to a gate to open it for parents.  This left one caregiver in charge of the group while the other caregiver was in and out of the cafeteria with the groups.

Child/ Caregiver Ratio: The classroom was out of ratio. There were 27 children to 1 caregiver, wiith the majority of the children being 4 years old.     Corrected:  13 children were picked up by their parents, before the inspection ended.

Child/ Caregiver Ratio: One caregiver was observed supervising alone 28 children aged 6 and up for approximately 30 minutes. This issue was resolved when two additional caregivers arrived, bringing the ratio into compliance.

Child/ Caregiver Ratio: There was one caregiver in a classroom with twenty-seven children. The children were on the floor watching a movie on the projector and playing games on the side. Several other caregivers arrived, and the twenty-seven children were broken up into small groups. The operation was able to correct the deficiency by splitting the children up into three groups with one caregiver in each group. The specific age is 4 10 years old.
